newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African local government told to sink or swim.
newsitem.headline: S.African local government told to sink or swim.

text.p: South Africa's central government will not bail out local authorities which run short of cash, the chief director of inter-governmental finance said on Thursday.

Ismail Momoniat told a budget forum organised by Old Mutual and Nedcor Ltd that local authorities had estimated total debts of 26 billion rand but added that he believed the media had exaggerated the extent of the financial crisis.

"Often the supposed crisis is linked to what is perceived to be a huge (rates) non-payment problem... but for example a big metro like Johannesburg is collecting close to 85 percent of its total revenue," he said.
"Central government has taken a very firm line (on the debt)," he said. "We will not pick up the tab... The message we are sending out is that they have to fend for themselves."
